institutionName: UiT The Arctic University of Norway

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: living in the Arctic

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy, orientation week at UiT is very comproehnisble and they point you at all necessary resources. Sometimes they can be a bit slow to e-mail.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Orientation week with most importnat information on the uni, registering in Norway, free-time possibilities

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Facebook groups are best I think to find short-term sublets

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Private housing can be quite expansive and often it does not include November/December as people rather rent out their rooms as AirBNBs  in the high tourist season

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not get student housing in the first place because they have limited amounts of places for international students. I applied early and it still didn't work, it seems a bit random how they make their decisions. I can recommend to just call because then they are super helpful and you have higher chances of getting a room.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You get detailed information on all online platforms and how to sign up for everything.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Website, FAQ, in-person student service

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I did get all the classes I wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Sign up for more courses in the beginning to have options later on. The scheduling can be quite weird and might overlap.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Level of courses are very good and really good quality of teaching

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There was less group work and in-class discussion compared to UCPH but otherwise very comparable with a lot of readings and lectures

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Climate Change Adaptation, Environmental Anthropology, Globalization: Values, Resources, and Power

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I really like the anthropology department at UiT, it has amazing teaching and very interesting courses. It is also quite small so all the teaching feels very personal.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Produce was very expensive, the rest very similar to copenhagen

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There is TSI, the student sport organiaztion where you can try a lot of different sports like sea-kayaking or cross country skiing. The uni has a lot of social clubs like board game club and the city in general is very catered towards students and stiudent-friendly activities.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: There are polar night morining cafes with free cofee and UV lamps which is really helpful to keep to your routine in the dark months.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: There are a lot of outdoor activities that you can do like hiking, kayaking, cross-country skiing. A lot of hiking is accessible per public transport. You can get a memebership to sleep in outdoor cabins which is super nice for weekend trips. And there is Turbo/BUA, where you can rent outdoor equipment for free and you only need to get a norwegian number

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy, very similiar to Denmark.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: The sports clubs and activities are a good opportunity to meet local students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The fun in outdoor activities and learning about sámi culture

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be sure to have a good routine during polar night and use the few hours of light to be outside, I did not have a lot of lectures but rather a lot of individual readings so find a good study group, do a lot of hiking or other outdoor activities

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Definetlely call the student housing organisation to have a better chance. I think it is always easier in the spring semester but in the winter semester it can be really tough.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Being outside in nature a lot

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The short days and exams during polar night

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
